minutes.headline: COA privately funds two summer concerts after override cut town band; explores senior outreach networks.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Council on Aging welcomed two new board members, reviewed donation-fund and program policies, and heard how two pavilion band concerts were arranged privately (without town funding) after the failed override eliminated town-sponsored band concerts. Much of the meeting concerned exploring new ways to reach housebound seniors, including a possible partnership with a regional volunteer-matching network and a national video-visit program, alongside a routine financial and director's report covering upcoming events, a hiring update, and a facility flooring renovation.

what_happened.line: Board members privately arranged two pavilion band concerts after the failed override ended town-funded band concerts.
The board agreed to explore forming a committee on a regional volunteer-matching model for housebound seniors, weighing its fee schedule.
Two new board members were formally welcomed and seated.
The director reported no funds spent yet this fiscal year; unspent COA money reverts to the town's general fund at year end.
A friendly visitor volunteer training session was scheduled for late July.

why_it_matters: Town-sponsored band concerts ended when the override failed; this summer's shows happened only because board members paid for them privately, with no guarantee for future years.
Pursuing the volunteer-matching network under consideration would mean a new recurring membership cost for the Council on Aging, which is only being explored, not yet decided.
COA funds not spent by year end return to the town's general fund rather than carrying over, a mechanism worth knowing when reading the department's year-end totals.
